items.title: (feature) add tensor chunk map compression: support strided representation (per-config) to save memory
items.body:
### PR Category
<!-- What kind of PR is this? Clean category helps keep PR small and review high quality.
     Available options: Feature, Performance, Bug fix, Cleanup, Test Only.
     Please include this in your PR title -->
Feature

### Summary
<!-- Explain the motivation for this change. What problem does it solve?
     To link an issue: Closes #<number>  /  Fixes #<number>  /  Relates to #<number> -->

#### Problem

KvChunkAddressTable serializes one proto entry per (slot, layer, position chunk). At production scale this hits protobuf's ~2GB message cap — the table simply cannot be written — and even below the cap it inflates file size, send time, and read/parse time (a 61-layer × 8-slot × 128k-seq table is 40MB / 1.95M entries; larger multi-config tables are worse).

#### Changes

New features include:
- compression, both in-memory and in file. 
- new format versioning
- support for dual-mode protobufs 
- lightweight chunk map reader (chunk_map_info.py)

A new protobuf definition was added (KvChunkRun + a per-config ChunkCompression tag): instead of one entry per (slot, layer, chunk), each row of the table is written as a few base+stride runs — chunk_step included, so block-cyclic bank rotation is just one affine stream per bank. A 40MB / ~2M-entry table comes out at ~12KB.

On the in-memory side the table now holds per-config maps in either the old materialized grid or the compressed strided form, and readers instantiate whichever the file declares. Consumers dispatch once per pass (visit_map/visit_range) and iterate the representation's native range — real span for unrolled, computing view for strided — so each form gets its own optimized loop instead of a runtime branch per lookup.

Also in the proto: format_version (absent = legacy; readers reject versions newer than they know instead of misparsing) and origin_host (which host wrote the file, for debugging). Plus tools/triage/chunk_map_info.py, a stdlib-only inspector that prints version, origin host, dims, compression tags, payload form and device groups for any .pb on any host — no protobuf or ttnn needed, and it reports unknown fields rather than misreading newer files.

chunk_map_info.py is a small inspector for the .pb files (tools/triage/chunk_map_info.py). It reads the protobuf wire format directly. It prints a summarized view of the protobuf file: format version, which host wrote it, per-config dims and compression tag, whether the payload is entries or runs, device groups and their hosts. --entries/--runs dump the raw records, --json for scripts.

#### Upgrade path

1. Readers first. Everything here is reader-side compatible by default; deploy this everywhere before writers emit runs-only.
2. Writers dual-write. Existing behavior by default — no flag needed; small tables carry both forms.
3. Runs-only only when no old readers remain (or never — the mirror is free below the threshold). The 2GB-cap tables that motivate this work are only writable/readable by the new code either way.


### Notes for reviewers
<!-- Where should reviewers focus? Call out anything non-obvious, tradeoffs, or areas of uncertainty. -->

items.title: [Feature] [Quasar] binary_ng: Quasar-native multi-DM / multi-Tensix support and typical case perf measurement
items.body:
### PR Category

Feature — experimental, opt-in, **off by default**.

### Summary

On Quasar a single metal `CoreCoord` is a whole cluster: **8 DM cores** (DM0 is the DFB ISR, DM1 the
remapper, so 6 usable) and **4 Neo compute cores**. The existing `experimental::quasar::binary_ng` port is
a 1:1 mirror of the Gen1 single-threaded structure, so it runs on 2 DM cores and 1 Neo and leaves the rest
of the cluster idle.

This adds a **third program factory** to the existing `program_factory_t` variant that spreads one op
across the cluster via `KernelSpec::num_threads` — `R` reader DM threads, `C` compute Neos, `W` writer DM
threads — with each DFB sized `entries_per_thread * max(its two endpoint counts)` so the STRIDED
sub-rings divide evenly.

**Measured on craq-sim** (bf16 `add`, TILE, DRAM-interleaved, no broadcast): `R=4, C=4, W=2` — the full
6-DM + 4-Neo budget — is **bit-exact** and delivers **4.00x** on the marginal basis, **2.70x** on the span
basis at the 1280-tile benchmark shape. 4.00x is exactly the theoretical ceiling: going `1,1,1 -> 4,4,2`
shrinks the reader term 4x, the compute term 4x and the writer term only 2x, so no cost model of the form
`max(Rc/R, Cc/C, Wc/W)` can exceed 4. The fitted model is `max(165.0/R, 176.5/C, 83.5/W)` cyc/tile and
agrees with all 31 legal configurations to within 0.04%.

Selection is a strict subset of the existing `matches_metal_v2_slice`, and its first test is a cached
bool that is false unless `TTNN_QSR_NATIVE` is set — so with the env var unset this is inert and the
`metal_v2` factory remains the default arm for every shape.

Also included: the research, design and status records under
`binary_ng/docs/QUASAR_NATIVE_{RESEARCH,DESIGN,STATUS}.md`, as an engineering record rather than user
documentation. The perf measurement data and analysis is in the status doc, and background info is in research and design doc.

### Notes for reviewers

Three things are outstanding:

1. **A substrate defect bounds what this can ship with.** Any configuration where a DFB's **DM** thread
   count exceeds its **Tensix** thread count silently returns wrong data — no hang, no error, and no
   measurable slowdown. That is **18 of the 31 legal `(R,C,W)` configurations**; the rule is
   `R <= C and W <= C`, and it holds 31/31 with zero disagreements. The `4,4,2` optimum is inside the
   good region and is bit-exact, so the headline result stands, but the general case does not.

   **This is not caused by this op.** It reproduces in `unit_tests_api` with no TTNN involvement, using
   the existing upstream DFB test kernels unmodified, in a `DM -> DFB -> Tensix -> DFB -> DM` pipeline at
   the same thread triples and with matching corruption fractions. A single DFB is correct at every one of
   those shapes, so the defect needs two DFBs chained through a Tensix stage that is simultaneously a
   consumer and a producer. Those gtest additions are **not in this PR** — they are going to the
   simulator team as the reproducer for a separate issue.

2. **craq-sim only.** No Wormhole or Blackhole validation, and none is meaningful — the factory is gated
   on `arch() == QUASAR`. craq-sim has no NoC, DRAM-bank or L1-port contention model, so the thread-count
   speedups above are an **upper bound** for silicon and the emulator campaign is still to come. The
   docs are explicit about which half of each number the simulator is trustworthy about.

3. **The slice is deliberately narrow.** bf16 `add` only, TILE only, tensor-tensor, no broadcast, no
   activations, no sharding, interleaved DRAM. Everything else falls through to the existing factories.
   `kernels_qsr/` holds only the no-broadcast FPU sources, and the factory `TT_FATAL`s rather than
   silently mis-running if the gate is ever widened without copying the rest.

items.title: [Performance] Reduce MeshWorkload host dispatch overhead
items.body:
### PR Category
Performance

### Summary
Repeated multi-program `MeshWorkload` enqueues were rebuilding stable topology and command-layout metadata on every operation. Cache the derived workload/device metadata, runtime-argument size, and direct circular-buffer patch destinations so the serial enqueue path only refreshes launch-time values.

This is the evidence-backed serial optimization from the investigation following #53562. The per-enqueue multithreaded fanout and experimental environment controls are intentionally not included because GLM's command streams were too small to amortize their synchronization cost.

On the equivalent experimental serial path:
- Local GLM-shaped enqueue p50: 24.07 µs → 20.39 µs (15.3% lower).
- Focused GLM CI host submission: 23.49 ms → 22.18 ms (5.6% lower).
- Chunk median: 1.666 s → 1.590 s (4.6% lower), though host submission is only about 1.4% of total chunk time, so this does not establish a stable end-to-end model speedup.

### Notes for reviewers
- `MeshWorkloadImpl` caches immutable post-finalization classifications and config sizes; sub-device IDs remain keyed by mesh and active manager.
- `MeshDeviceImpl` owns the device-range lookup cache and invalidates it on reshape.
- Circular-buffer command patch destinations are cached when commands are assembled. `UpdateCircularBufferPageSize` updates both normal and trace-cached sequences, and enqueue preserves local and remote CB validation.
- Full-mesh workloads avoid building/scanning the unused-device set; partial workloads retain the existing GO-signal path.

Validation:
- `~/bin-metal/build_metal_cpp.sh`
- `pre-commit run --from-ref origin/main --to-ref HEAD`
- `MeshWorkloadTestSuite.MeshWorkloadCBUpdate` (fast dispatch)
- `MeshDeviceFixture.TensixTestUpdateCircularBufferPageSize` (slow dispatch)

items.title: Let a spec factory build a different program per mesh coordinate
items.body:
Right now a spec factory gets asked for its `ProgramArtifacts` exactly once, and the adapter maps that one `ProgramSpec` onto every range of the mesh. That's fine for SPMD, but it means two things are impossible today: an op whose program differs per device, and an op that wants the same program everywhere with different run args per device. Both keep coming up as "needs TTNN infra support" when people look at porting ops to the Metal 2.0 spec path.

The metal side isn't the problem — `MakeMeshWorkloadFromSpecs` already takes a range-to-spec map and has been tested running distinct specs on distinct devices. The adapter just never had a way for a factory to say "ask me per coordinate".

So that's all this adds. `create_program_artifacts` can now take a `MeshCoordinate`:

```cpp
static ProgramArtifacts create_program_artifacts(
    const operation_attributes_t&, const tensor_args_t&, tensor_return_value_t&,
    const std::optional<ttnn::MeshCoordinate>&);
```

Declare that signature and the adapter calls you once per coordinate; each call returns its own spec, its own run args and its own op-owned tensors. Don't declare it and nothing changes — one call, mapped onto every occupied range, same as before.

Detection is by signature, the same way `create_descriptor` already decides whether it wants the coordinate. That was deliberate: no new factory concept, so the "exactly one concept per `program_factory_t` alternative" rule is untouched and nothing about how existing factories classify changes. I also made an empty spec at a coordinate mean "no work here" and skip it, matching what the descriptor path does, so an MPMD op can legitimately leave some devices idle.

One thing worth knowing if you write a custom-flavor factory: the cache-miss path applies the run args that came out of `create_program_artifacts`, not the ones from `override_runtime_arguments`. The override only runs on hits. So if your run args vary per device, they have to come from a per-coordinate `create_program_artifacts` — otherwise the first dispatch gets mesh-wide args and every later one gets per-device args, which is a nasty thing to debug. Noted in the header.

Not in here: GlobalSemaphore. The spec API only has program-scoped `SemaphoreSpec` today, so ops that need cross-device sync (CCL and friends) are still blocked on the metal side regardless of this change. Separate problem, separate owner.

### Testing

The gtest additions are compile-coverage, following what's already in that file: per-coordinate factories for both spec flavors, static_asserts that taking the coordinate doesn't change which flavor a factory classifies as, and the detection predicate pinned in both directions so a future refactor can't silently flip everything onto one path.

I checked the new branch is actually reachable rather than assuming it: shadowed the header with a copy containing a deliberate error inside the per-coordinate branch and confirmed it fails to compile, and fails *only* for the two per-coordinate factories. `if constexpr` branches that nothing instantiates are easy to fool yourself about.

What this does **not** have is any runtime coverage — no op takes the coordinate yet, so nothing dispatches through the new path. That comes with the first real per-coord op, and I'd rather land the mechanism first than invent a fake op to exercise it.

items.title: Fix physical chip access in memory benchmark
items.body:
### PR Category
Bug fix

### Summary

Memory benchmark crashes after this change https://github.com/tenstorrent/tt-metal/pull/54238

items.title: [Bug fix] Fix LLK tests so single-bank kernels work regardless of DRAM bank count
items.body:
### PR Category
Bug fix

### Summary
Some LLK tests use reader and writer kernels that only ever touch one DRAM bank 0. However, the tests built each buffer with one page per tile, with the pages being interleaved across every DRAM bank.

With only one DRAM bank, this made no difference. Every tile still landed in bank 0, so the kernels worked.

With more than one DRAM bank, only some tiles landed in bank 0. The kernels read the wrong tiles, in the wrong order.

This change gives each buffer one page for the whole buffer, not one page per tile. A buffer with one page always sits in a single bank.

items.title: [Bug Fix] Fix mul reduce scalar zero-flag initialization
items.body:
### PR Category
Bug fix

### Summary
- Restore the format-default source zero-flag state in experimental mul_reduce_scalar initialization on Wormhole and Blackhole.
- Prevent a preceding copy_init() from leaking PRESERVE mode into GAPOOL/MVMUL operations.
- Add a directed BF16-denormal regression test.

copy_init() configures ALU_ACC_CTRL_Zero_Flag_disabled_src to preserve denormal inputs. Unlike the standard reduce and block_max_row paths,  _llk_math_mul_reduce_scalar_init_() did not restore the format-derived default before executing its FPU reduction operations.

On silicon this changes denormal handling. TTSim rejects the leaked state with:

UnsupportedFunctionality: tensix_matmul_op: ALU_ACC_CTRL_Zero_Flag_disabled_src=1 (keep SrcB denormals) not modeled

Call _configure_default_zero_flag_state_() from the WH and BH scalar-reduce initialization paths. This follows the state-management contract already used by the other compute operations while preserving the behavior of copy_init() itself.

The new test:

- enters through the copy-based sum_reduce_scalar path, establishing PRESERVE state;
- uses the largest finite BF16 input and smallest BF16 subnormal scaler;
- verifies that the compute-default state flushes the scaler and produces exactly zero.

The test passes with this change and reproduces the original TTSim error when run against the pre-fix LLK source.

Closes #53055

items.title: Bring up FIBO VLM
items.body:
As part of the [FIBO image generation model](https://huggingface.co/briaai/FIBO) its [vision transformer](https://huggingface.co/briaai/FIBO-vlm) used for generating the prompt JSON is needed.

The VLM is a Qwen3-VL model based on the class `Qwen3VLForConditionalGeneration`.
